_meta.source: Written for claudeDM (Horror category). Original content; a few general-mechanics sentences (opportunity attacks, death saves, conditions) are adapted from SRD 5.1, licensed CC BY 4.0 — see NOTICE.
_meta.notes: Horror weapons and armor, 1890s, 1920s and 1970s. 'weapons' is a flat array in the Western shape; every weapon lists its 'eras' from 1890s, 1920s and 1970s (the three decades are not contiguous: each campaign sits in one). Every firearm and bow also carries 'ammo_name', the counted equipment line its ammunition is recorded under on a sheet (e.g. ".38 rounds (18)", "Shotgun shells (10)", "Arrows (20)"); melee weapons and the two Improvised weapons have none (a kerosene bottle or a stick of dynamite is itself the counted item, e.g. "Kerosene bottle (2)"). Costs are period dollars in a 'cost' string, by era where they differ. There are no automatic weapons and no fanning: every firearm fires single shots, and the double-barrel shotgun can fire both barrels. The properties silver, iron and fire matter because adversaries can be vulnerable to them (adversaries.json vulnerable_to; combat.json fighting_the_supernatural). Armor keeps the Western 'armor' object shape: two light coats and one medium vest, and the heavy, powered and shields lists are deliberately empty. Most people wear no armor: AC 10 + DEX. Gear and ammunition boxes are in gear.json.

weapons.name: Kitchen knife
weapons.notes: A carving or butcher's knife from any kitchen drawer. Everyone has one within reach, which is why it turns up in so many stories.

weapons.name: Scalpel
weapons.notes: A surgeon's blade from a doctor's bag or an embalmer's kit. Very sharp, very small, and not meant for this.

weapons.name: Silver knife
weapons.notes: A silver fruit knife, letter opener or dagger from a family service, kept sharp by someone who knew why. Silver: a creature vulnerable to silver takes double damage from it, and it ignores a resistance that does not apply to silver (combat.json fighting_the_supernatural). Soft metal: on a natural 1 the blade bends and is useless until straightened (a short rest and a vise).

weapons.name: Walking stick
weapons.notes: A cane or blackthorn stick. Nobody asks why a guest carries one indoors.

weapons.name: Fire iron
weapons.notes: A poker from beside the hearth, cold iron with a hooked end. Iron: a creature vulnerable to iron takes double damage from it, and it ignores a resistance that does not apply to iron (combat.json fighting_the_supernatural). Every house with a fireplace has one.

weapons.name: Crowbar
weapons.notes: A forged iron pry bar for crates, boards, coffin lids and doors. Iron (as the fire iron). Versatile: 1d8 when swung in two hands, applied at the table; the sheet records the one-handed 1d6. Gives advantage on STR checks to force or pry something open (gear.json).

weapons.name: Hatchet
weapons.notes: A camp or kindling hatchet. Can be thrown as a ranged attack (normal range 20 ft, long range 60 ft) using STR, and picked up again afterward. The head is steel, not iron: it does not count as iron.

weapons.name: Wood axe
weapons.notes: A felling axe from the woodpile. Heavy: a wielder with STR below 13 has disadvantage on attack rolls with it. It goes through a door in three turns (combat.json cover.destroying_cover).

weapons.name: Machete
weapons.notes: A long brush knife for clearing scrub and cane, sold in farm and hardware stores from the 1920s. Cuts through corn stalks, brush and rope as part of a move.

weapons.name: Torch
weapons.notes: A stick wrapped in oil-soaked rag, or a burning branch from the fire. Bright light in a 20-ft radius and dim light 20 ft beyond for 1 hour (dread.json light_and_dark). Fire: deals fire damage, and a creature vulnerable to fire takes double. Can set flammable things alight (combat.json fire). Dropped in water, it goes out.

weapons.name: Pocket revolver
weapons.notes: A small five-shot .32 revolver for a coat pocket, a handbag or a doctor's bag. Reloading the cylinder takes an action (combat.json ammunition.reload).

weapons.name: Service revolver
weapons.notes: A six-shot .38 revolver of the kind carried by police, soldiers and night watchmen in every era. Reloading the cylinder takes an action.

weapons.name: .45 automatic
weapons.notes: A heavy semi-automatic pistol with a seven-round magazine, army issue since before the Great War. Swapping a magazine is a bonus action, if you have a loaded one: spare magazines are gear.json items and are filled from your .45 rounds.

weapons.name: Flare pistol
weapons.notes: A wide-bore signal pistol from a boat or a lifeboat locker. Fired upward, a flare lights a 200-ft radius as bright light for 1 minute and is seen for miles (the boat may come). Fired at a creature, it is a ranged attack dealing 1d6 fire damage, and the target catches fire (combat.json fire) on a hit; a creature vulnerable to fire takes double.

weapons.name: Lever-action rifle
weapons.notes: A tube-fed lever rifle in .30 calibre: farm gun, deer gun, a gun that has been in a hall closet for forty years. An action loads four rounds through the side gate (combat.json ammunition.reload).

weapons.name: Hunting rifle
weapons.notes: A bolt-action deer and elk rifle, often with a telescopic sight in the 1970s. An action loads all five rounds from a stripper clip or by hand.

weapons.name: Double-barrel shotgun
weapons.notes: A side-by-side 12-gauge: bird gun, varmint gun, the gun over the farmhouse door. Firing both barrels at once is one attack as an action (combat.json fire_modes.both_barrels). Breaking it open and loading both shells takes an action.

weapons.name: Pump shotgun
weapons.notes: A slide-action 12-gauge with a tube magazine. An action loads two shells into the tube.

weapons.name: Crossbow
weapons.notes: A hunting or target crossbow with a cranked or levered string. Drawing and loading a bolt is a bonus action. Quiet: heard only within 30 ft (combat.json noise). A bolt can be tipped with silver (gear.json) to count as silver.

weapons.name: Hunting bow
weapons.notes: A wood or fiberglass hunting bow. It is drawn, not loaded: nocking an arrow is part of the attack, and its magazine of 1 means each shot spends one counted arrow. Quiet, as the crossbow. An arrow can be tipped with silver (gear.json) to count as silver.

weapons.name: Kerosene bottle
weapons.cost: $0.10 (a bottle, a rag and a pint of kerosene)
weapons.notes: A bottle of lamp oil with a burning rag in the neck. Lighting it is a bonus action. Thrown at a point within range, it bursts in a 5-ft radius: each creature there makes a DEX save (DC 12, no proficiency needed), taking 2d6 fire damage on a failure or half on a success, and the area burns for 1 minute (combat.json fire). A creature vulnerable to fire takes double. Carry it as a counted equipment item, e.g. "Kerosene bottle (2)"; it is not written in a sheet's weapons list.

weapons.name: Dynamite
weapons.notes: One stick of dynamite from a quarry, a farm (for stumps) or a construction site. Lighting the fuse is a bonus action; it goes off at the start of your next turn. 10-ft radius: each creature makes a DEX save (DC 12, or 8 + proficiency + DEX if the thrower is proficient in Mechanics), taking 3d6 bludgeoning on a failure or half on a success. It brings down a doorway, a ceiling or a crypt mouth (combat.json explosives). Carry it as a counted equipment item, e.g. "Dynamite (2)"; it is not written in a sheet's weapons list.

weapon_groups.Melee: Knives, sticks, fire irons, crowbars, hatchets, axes, a machete, a torch, fists and anything else in reach. Everyone is proficient.
weapon_groups.Sidearms: Revolvers, the .45 automatic and the flare pistol: the guns that fit in a pocket, a holster, a glove box or a nightstand drawer.
weapon_groups.Longarms: Rifles and shotguns: the lever-action, the hunting rifle and the two shotguns. Two-handed.
weapon_groups.Bows: The hunting bow and the crossbow: quiet, slow and good for silver-tipped shafts. Only the Hunter starts proficient.
weapon_groups.Improvised: The kerosene bottle and dynamite. Throwing one needs no proficiency, because it is a DEX save, not an attack roll; no class lists this group, and these items are carried as counted equipment, not written in a sheet's weapons list (combat.json explosives, fire).

weapon_properties.concealable: Small enough to hide in a pocket, a handbag, a boot or a sleeve. Spotting it takes a pat-down or a Perception check against the carrier's Sleight of Hand.
weapon_properties.finesse: Use STR or DEX for attack and damage rolls (the same for both).
weapon_properties.heavy: Big and hard to swing. A wielder with STR below 13 has disadvantage on attack rolls with it.
weapon_properties.loud: A gunshot is heard all through a house, across a farm and half a mile over water at night. Everything in the dark knows where you are (combat.json noise), and the muzzle flash ruins your night sight for a moment (combat.json darkness_and_light).
weapon_properties.quiet: Heard only within 30 ft, and not through a closed door.
weapon_properties.scatter: Fires a spread of shot. +2 to hit targets within 30 ft. At long range you have disadvantage and lose the +2. Apply the +2 at the table; it is not part of the attack bonus written on a sheet.
weapon_properties.two-handed: Requires two hands to fire or swing. You can't hold a lantern and fire it; a light-source in the other hand means one-handed use at disadvantage.
weapon_properties.versatile (1d8): Can be used in one or two hands. In two hands it deals 1d8 instead of its listed die. The sheet records the listed (one-handed) die; apply the versatile die at the table.
weapon_properties.thrown (20/60): A melee weapon that can also be thrown as a ranged attack: normal range 20 ft, long range 60 ft (disadvantage), using the same ability as its melee attack. The hatchet.
weapon_properties.thrown: Thrown at a point rather than a creature, using the listed range; creatures in the area make a DEX save (combat.json explosives, fire).
weapon_properties.silver: Made of silver. A creature vulnerable to silver takes double damage from it, and a creature that resists ordinary weapons takes full damage from it unless its resistance says otherwise (combat.json fighting_the_supernatural).
weapon_properties.iron: Cold iron. A creature vulnerable to iron takes double damage from it, and a creature that resists ordinary weapons takes full damage from it unless its resistance says otherwise.
weapon_properties.fire: Deals or starts fire. A creature vulnerable to fire takes double damage. Fire spreads (combat.json fire).
weapon_properties.light-source: Gives light: the torch while it burns (bright light 20 ft, dim 20 ft beyond), the flare pistol when fired (dread.json light_and_dark).

light.name: Heavy coat
light.notes: A thick wool overcoat, a sheepskin-lined work coat, a pea coat or a farm jacket: whatever keeps out the cold where you come from. It turns a knife, blunts a bite and takes the worst out of a fall; against a bullet it is only a coat. Pockets hold a revolver, a flashlight, a box of shells and a fistful of salt. The coat a generated character wears by default.

light.name: Leather jacket
light.notes: A leather work or driving coat in the 1890s, a flyer's or motorcyclist's jacket in the 1920s, a biker's or a farmhand's in the 1970s. Tough, quiet and waterproof enough. In a good parlor it marks you as someone who works with their hands.

medium.name: Padded vest
medium.notes: A thick quilted vest: a fencing or baseball catcher's pad, a layered canvas vest a smith stitched with metal plates, a 1970s police flak vest. It stops a dog's teeth and a slashing claw and slows a pistol bullet. Stiff and loud: disadvantage on Stealth checks. Obvious under a coat to anyone who touches you.

currency.note: Horror campaigns use dollars and cents. Money on a character sheet is a single equipment line written exactly as shown in 'sheet_format'. Prices are period dollars and differ by era: a meal 25 cents in 1893, 50 cents in 1924, $2 in 1974; a night in a hotel $1 / $3 / $15; a .38 revolver $12 / $28 / $110. Cost strings give each era's price where it differs.
